answers.text: Give it a fixed format: line 1 drop-off time, line 2 pallet count, line 3 any damage noted, always in that order. If the driver's message doesn't mention damage, write 'none noted' rather than skipping the line.
Structure: time, customer, topic, outcome for every entry, then count up how many need a follow-up call at the end. Same format for everyone.

The finishing time doesn't work — if they start at 8am and it's roughly six hours, that's done early afternoon the same day, not the next one. The note says the 23rd, which is a day out. I'd double-check that before it's filed.
Invoices up from 96 to 118 — that's a fair jump this month.
I'd sign off Output 2, since it shows the actual ticket numbers behind the 88%. Output 1 doesn't show where the number came from.
I'd probably go with the second one, it sounds more thought through.
1. No, that's an employee's home address, definitely not. 2. Yes, that's fine. 3. No, that budget hasn't been signed off. 4. Probably not, it's still their document. 5. No, that's personal.
I'd hold back the hourly rates and retainer cap, and be careful with the non-disclosure clause since it names the client. Not sure about the rest.
I'd spot-check some of the reconciled figures against the warehouse system before the summary goes out, rather than just reading it over.

The riskiest step is reading the invoice PDF and pulling out the line items — get that wrong and everything downstream is wrong. The real gate needs to sit before the payment note is auto-submitted, checking that the extracted total is actually within a sensible tolerance of the PO amount.
